bullets.title: IBM Q2 miss drags enterprise software — NOW, CRM, SNOW, PLTR, ADBE hammered
bullets.body: IBM pre-announced Q2 revenue of $17.20B vs $17.86B consensus and EPS of $2.93 vs $3.01, blaming capex reprioritization toward servers/storage and large deals failing to close. The miss cascaded across enterprise software: NOW -7.8%, CRM -6.1%, WDAY -8.9%, HUBS -8.9%, SNOW -4.7%, MDB -4.4%, ADBE -5.5%, PLTR -5.2% in pre-market. IBM was downgraded to Reduce at HSBC (PT cut to $191 from $231); UBS notes NOW demand trends are stable with no material improvement, maintaining Neutral at 19x '26 FCF; GS is a buyer of CRM into 3Q on 5x higher agent usage and Slack strength.

bullets.title: AAPL: KeyBanc downgrades to Underweight, $250 PT; Morgan Stanley stays OW at $360
bullets.body: KeyBanc cut Apple to Underweight from Sector Weight (PT $250, ~21% downside from $317) citing slowing iPhone builds, weak US upgrade rates, carrier subsidy pullback, and Services deceleration risk to ~7% in FY27 vs consensus ~12%. Separately, Morgan Stanley reiterates OW at $360, noting the $200 iPhone 18 price hike is now more likely than prior $100-150 estimate and would drive 2-4% C3Q26 EPS upside. AAPL hit record highs the prior session as a relative safe-haven.

bullets.title: NVDA: Asia buyer list halved on China export controls; Mitsubishi Heavy partnership announced
bullets.body: The FT reported Nvidia cut its permitted buyer list in Singapore, Malaysia, and Japan by 50%+ to prevent Chinese companies from circumventing export controls. Separately, Nikkei reported NVDA is considering adopting Mitsubishi Heavy's cooling and energy management technology for next-gen data center plants. Wolfe names NVDA its Alpha Pick with >$1tn Blackwell/Rubin order visibility through CY27; JPM's Chips for Breakfast notes Vera Rubin PCB is in mass production with Kyber NVL144 rack under testing.

bullets.title: META: Bullish sentiment builds on AI monetization credibility; +20% rally in two weeks
bullets.body: JPM's Anmuth says META has shifted the investor debate from 'how to monetize AI' to 'how much,' supporting a +20% rally in two weeks. 2027 capex is expected at $200-225B (up ~$75B Y/Y with some estimates to $275B), and a potential equity raise is likely if stock sustains above $700. Citi options flow shows META 1M implied vol at 1Y highs (52.8 IV, 55.7 RV) following 9% w/w gain; META API pricing estimated at ~25% of OpenAI/Anthropic costs. A potential equity raise cited as near-term watch item.

bullets.title: AMZN: Top internet pick into earnings — 54% Prime Day strength, AWS backlog near $500B
bullets.body: Jefferies and JPM both flag AMZN as a top pick; survey shows 54% of shoppers spent >10% more YoY on Prime Days. AWS backlog accelerating from 93% y/y in Q1, approaching ~$500B. AMZN trades at 12x NTM EV/EBITDA vs WMT at 19x and GOOGL at 17x, below its 18x 10-year average. Buy rating at JPM with $320 PT; JPM 2027 capex modeled at ~$300B (+42% vs consensus).

bullets.title: NFLX: Morgan Stanley reiterates OW but cuts PT to $90 from $115 on sentiment/estimate drag
bullets.body: MS lowered PT to $90 (~22x NTM EPS, vs prior 30x) on ~4% EPS cuts for FY27/28, citing engagement hour growth decelerating to low-single digits and a larger-than-usual post-price-hike churn spike (+50-100bps 2H26 US estimate). Bull case $115, bear case $60. Valuation seen as compelling at <20x fwd P/E for 20%+ EPS CAGR; new initiatives (live sports, third-party streaming bundles, AI cost savings of 20-40%) remain underpriced. NFLX reports Thursday July 16 after close with consensus EPS $0.79, revenue $12.58B.

bullets.title: TXN: Citi initiates Buy with C26/C27 EPS 4%/13% above consensus on data center power wins
bullets.body: Citi initiates TXN at Buy ahead of Jul-22 earnings; C26/C27 EPS of $8.03/$10.10 are 4%/13% above consensus. Data center revenue expected to double in 2026 (~50% CAGR 2025-2028) driven by 800V DC transition and NVIDIA Stage 1/2 socket ramps. Jun-Q/Sep-Q modeled at $5.3B/$5.7B sales, 1%/4% above consensus. Wolfe also upgraded TXN last summer on capex cycle inflection; now at 25x C27 FCF after 70% run.

bullets.title: AMD: Wolfe and Jefferies see $25+ EPS power from MI-450 and agentic CPU wins
bullets.body: Wolfe raises AMD FY27 estimates to $15 EPS, well ahead of street, with path to $25+ from two potential AI accelerator wins ($3-4/share per GW) and agentic CPU growth ($7/share). Citi notes AMD is preferred over INTC; INTC caution driven by difficulty building 2027 EPS at >$100/share. Jefferies' base EPS for AMD is $15 for next year.

bullets.title: INTU: Piper Sandler initiates Underweight, $250 PT on TurboTax and Desktop headwinds
bullets.body: Piper Sandler's Billy Fitzsimmons assumes INTU at Underweight with $250 PT (vs current ~$290), expecting below-consensus FY27 guidance and downward long-term target revisions at September investor day. Risks include TurboTax pricing/packaging changes, Desktop declines, and flat Mailchimp growth not reflected in consensus.

bullets.title: TSEM: Silicon photonics expansion sends stock +19% in pre-market
bullets.body: Tower Semiconductor announced expansion of silicon photonics and silicon germanium capacity; Jefferies notes TSEM is targeting $3.6B revenue and $1.2B net profit in 2028, 13% above street on revenue. The stock surged ~19% in pre-market. Morgan Stanley includes TSEM among key CPO/coherent optical supply chain participants alongside COHR and LITE.

bullets.title: AVGO: Morgan Stanley reiterates OW; maintains ~80% TPU share despite MediaTek competition
bullets.body: MS says AVGO retains ~80% of Google's TPU share; MediaTek's participation is real but not disruptive given HBM supply constraints, packaging execution, and scale advantages. AVGO remains a core AI winner with ASIC leadership and new customer ramps. PT $502 with OW rating. KeyBanc Asia takeaways note AVGO's INTC foundry wins (AWS Trainium 3, Google TPU) as supportive.

bullets.title: RDDT, CART, ABNB, DASH, UBER: Jefferies and JPM bullish into 2Q earnings
bullets.body: Jefferies' JC rates ABNB, CART, RDDT, UBER, DASH as top internet picks into 2Q on low valuations and margin upside; RDDT stands out on strong advertising demand and revenue upside. Cautious on LYFT (booking deceleration), EBAY (slowing GMV), and BKNG (elevated concerns). ABNB and EXPE well positioned to beat and potentially raise guidance. KeyBanc cuts UBER PT to $105 (from $110) and DASH PT to $275 (from $280) on conservative multiple framework while keeping Buy ratings.

bullets.title: CVNA: JPM maintains OW, $93 PT; modest 2Q beat expected with 35% unit growth
bullets.body: JPM models CVNA 2Q26 EBITDA of $785M (+$20M vs prior) driven by higher non-GAAP retail GPU of $3.5K. Unit growth tracking ~35% in June with no deceleration. 2027 EBITDA estimated at $4.3B ($3.9K/unit) on ~25x FY2 EV/EBITDA; PT implies line-of-sight to $7+ EPS by 2030. Off-lease supply inflection expected to benefit CVNA's independent dealer model.

bullets.title: DKNG: 2Q EBITDA trimmed to $115M on unfavorable World Cup holds; PM market growing 3x
bullets.body: OpCo and desk trim DKNG 2Q EBITDA to $115M (from $157M prior) due to unfavorable Knicks/World Cup sports outcomes despite handle up ~20% YoY. Prediction market volume hit ~$250M consumer/$750M total in June (3x May), expected to step up into NFL season. CFTC's looser regulatory approach seen supporting higher unit revenues. No change expected to $200-300M PM spending outlook on 2Q calls.

bullets.title: EQIX OW, DLR EW: Morgan Stanley sees data center moratoriums benefiting colocation REITs
bullets.body: MS research finds ~$156B of data center projects cancelled/delayed in 2025; $130B already delayed in 1Q26. Local opposition driven by power bill impacts, water use, and quality-of-life concerns. Colocation REITs (EQIX OW, DLR EW) insulated due to smaller scale vs. hyperscale; onsite generation adoption to benefit BE and SEI (both OW rated).

bullets.title: NOW: UBS Neutral; demand stable but no inflection, PT raised to $115 on 16x CY27 FCF
bullets.body: UBS maintains Neutral on ServiceNow; customer checks show stable but not improving 2Q demand with no step-change in AI-driven spend. Expects normal ~100bps cRPO beat. PT raised to $115 from $100 based on 16x CY27E FCF. AI Control Tower adoption remains modest; shares +20% off late-June lows driven by defensive tech rotation, not fundamentals.

bullets.title: PSKY/WBD: CA AG files TRO; tender offer extended to July 22
bullets.body: California AG Rob Bonta filed for a temporary restraining order to block the PSKY-WBD merger. Historical precedent (Nexstar/Tegna) suggests deals can close before TRO is granted. PSKY up 0.8% and WBD up 1.5% after exchange and tender offer expiration extended to July 22.

bullets.title: MU: IBD Top 50 ranked #1; bullish options flow; $3B US supply chain investment
bullets.body: MU ranked #1 on IBD Top 50 with multi-week consolidation pattern at 50-day moving average; price targets of $1,100-$1,200 cited for breakout. Large bullish options tape noted. Separately, MU announced $3B additional US semiconductor investment to secure HBM supply for AI growth. Citi semis roundtable notes memory fundamentals structurally bullish into H1:27; investors prefer NAND over DRAM due to HBM de-spec risk.

bullets.title: HOOD: First ABS offering gauged at $400M+; Robinhood Chain tops 750K accounts
bullets.body: Robinhood is reportedly gauging investor interest in its first asset-backed securities offering (~$400M+) backed by its branded credit card program. Robinhood Chain daily cumulative accounts crossed 750K. No rating change; these are potential capital markets catalysts.

bullets.title: CRCL: Mizuho downgrades to Underperform, PT $50 on Open-USD competitive threat
bullets.body: Mizuho cuts CRCL to Underperform from Neutral with PT slashed to $50 from $85, citing the Open-USD consortium (backed by Mastercard, Stripe, Coinbase, BlackRock) which routes nearly all reserve income to distributors vs. Circle's float-capture model retaining ~38%. CRCL 2027 adj. EBITDA revised to $699M (~25% below consensus); distribution costs rise from 64% to 73%. Coinbase revenue-sharing agreement renewal in August creates additional leverage risk.
